current_experience: Can wire basic circuits and use entry-level CAD.

sessions.student_message: Which catalog option best fits my interest in circuits, and what prerequisite is listed?
sessions.expected_behavior: Name Electronics and Circuit Design with both alternative prerequisites and a catalog citation. Explicitly connect the response to Introduction to Engineering (grade 9), Electronics Fundamentals (grade 10) and Engineering Design (grade 11). Use stated marks only if useful.

follow_ups.student_message: Switching topics, I might like animation. Suggest a simple movement study with paper and pencil.
follow_ups.expected_behavior: Treat animation as the current interest. Suggest one project, connect it to at least one applicable course per grade year when useful, and avoid framing it as the prior interest or changing the saved profile.

sessions.student_message: Show a worked example of using Ohm's law with a 9 V source and a 3 ohm resistor.
sessions.expected_behavior: Use Ohm's law accurately and label the result in amperes. Explicitly connect the response to Introduction to Engineering (grade 9), Electronics Fundamentals (grade 10) and AP Physics 1 (grade 11). Use stated marks only if useful.

follow_ups.student_message: If the resistance doubled and the voltage stayed the same, what would happen to the current?
follow_ups.expected_behavior: Apply the inverse relationship accurately and identify the fixed voltage.

sessions.student_message: Create a two-action study plan to improve my circuit diagram skills.
sessions.expected_behavior: Suggest two small actions that target circuit diagrams. Explicitly connect the response to Introduction to Engineering (grade 9), Electronics Fundamentals (grade 10) and Engineering Design (grade 11). Use stated marks only if useful.

follow_ups.student_message: How can I tell whether the first action actually improved my diagrams?
follow_ups.expected_behavior: Give a simple check tied to diagram accuracy.

sessions.student_message: I drew two diagrams, but I still mix up series and parallel layouts. What should I practice next?
sessions.expected_behavior: Acknowledge completed diagrams and address the series/parallel distinction. Explicitly connect the response to Introduction to Engineering (grade 9), Electronics Fundamentals (grade 10) and AP Physics 1 (grade 11). Use stated marks only if useful. Carry forward a concrete relevant detail from the earlier circuits discussion when it helps, and keep the intervening animation topic out of the answer.

follow_ups.student_message: Can I trace the wires with a pencil to see where the path branches?
follow_ups.expected_behavior: Explain how tracing distinguishes a branch from one continuous path.

sessions.student_message: How could I make a three-photo series about shapes around my home?
sessions.expected_behavior: Address photography as the active interest and suggest a manageable starting project.

follow_ups.student_message: What could tie the three photos together even if I use different objects?
follow_ups.expected_behavior: Suggest a shared visual element such as shape, framing, or light.

sessions.student_message: Both bulbs are drawn next to each other, but I can trace only one route. How should I label that layout?
sessions.expected_behavior: Infer the circuit diagrams. Explain that one path indicates series when components share it, regardless of physical position.

follow_ups.student_message: What would I have to change in the wiring to make the drawing show two paths?
follow_ups.expected_behavior: Explain a branch in the diagram rather than physical placement.

sessions.student_message: Help me compare two bulb diagrams, one with a single path and one with two branches.
sessions.expected_behavior: Answer the new task while using relevant saved profile or earlier context.

follow_ups.student_message: How can I check whether the wires share a single path even if the bulbs are drawn side by side?
follow_ups.expected_behavior: Use the just-discussed setup and answer the detail without restarting the whole task.

follow_ups.student_message: How should I label a layout with a single current path? Separately, how could I show movement in four pencil drawings?
follow_ups.expected_behavior: Correctly identify series and switch to an independent animation exercise.
